MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  February 25, 2020

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:01 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of the Silver Spur Little League led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – FIRST QUARTER 2020

  On behalf of Waste Management, Sharon Shapiro-Fox provided an update on the
  services available to residents this spring, including the upcoming Free Paper Shredding
  event that will be held at the City’s Earth Day Celebration on April 22, 2020. She then
  drew names for this quarter’s “Recycling Hero” winners of one year of free refuse service:

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 7 PLEASANT HILL DRIVE
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: ROLLING HILLS INVESTMENTS

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  City Manager Greg Grammer noted that Item 5I was previously reviewed and approved
  by the Council on the February 11, 2020 City Council Agenda, and suggested it be
  removed from the consent calendar.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-H & J APPROVED AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 11, 2020

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
 C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 11, 2020

  APPROVED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – FEBRUARY 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62458 THROUGH 62507 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $316,061.39 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020520 THROUGH 020620;
  62377(VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,988.48 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $392,049.87 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT - JANUARY 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT - JANUARY 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA REGIONAL EMERGENCY  PREPAREDNESS
  COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 14, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

H.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 14, 2019

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

J.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 30, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  PRESENTATION ON ALERT SOUTHBAY - A REGIONAL INTEGRATED EMERGENCY
  ALERT AND WARNING NOTIFICATION SYSTEM

  Alert Southbay Representative Soraya Sutherland introduced Alert Southbay, a regional
  alert and warning notification system that will replace Nixel to alert residents about local
  incidents, emergencies and disasters. Ms. Sutherland outlined the software, its capabilities,
  and what the community can expect once the upgrade to Alert Southbay is made.

  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis explained the transition, and noted that residents
  currently opted into Nixel will automatically be transitioned over and do not need to re-
  register.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the cost of the software, Ms.
  Sutherland explained that the funding for this program comes from each of the participating
  cities.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that there is an oversight board made up of
  representatives from each participating city.

  Assistant City Manager Davis and Ms. Sutherland further explained the capabilities and
  benefits of Alert Southbay during severe emergencies within the area.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Sutherland explained the flow of
  information through the system, from the initial 911 call to the alerts going out to residents.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN asked for clarification on the cost of this program, which
  Assistant City Manager Davis explained will be nearly equivalent to that of the City’s current
  Nixel contract.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that the fee the City pays for this service is
  based on population size.

  Discussion ensued regarding the number of subscribers, and the City’s plans for community
  outreach to notify residents on social media platforms. It was also suggested to have a booth
  at the City’s Earth Day Celebration in April for residents to get more information about the
  system and to sign up.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL emphasized that this new platform will be much more
  informative and useful to residents.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the
  training referenced in the presentation is intended for City staff, which includes four trainings
  per month for the next two years.

  Carmelo Sorce from CalWater provided a construction update on the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Mr. Sorce discussed the water main break on
  Palos Verdes Drive North on February 24, 2020.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN emphasized that this water main break occurred on the
  old pipe system. He then asked when the switch from the old infrastructure to the new
  infrastructure would take place, which Mr. Sorce confirmed would be the middle of this year.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that he is hearing from the community that
  residents are getting weary of this long project.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL, Mr. Sorce confirmed that the project on the
  Crenshaw line will be completed by mid-March. COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL also
  emphasized the necessity of this project.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  confirmed there was no risk of a sink hole resulting from the water main break.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Sorce explained that water pressure
  would not be changing, that the new lines are being tested in sections with both water and
  air, and that the majority of the new system will be put into service all at once.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF JANUARY
  21, 2020 - 2020-2025 SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached revised Agreement with
  Silver Spur Little League for use of Ernie Howlett Park's sports fields.

  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL City Attorney Davis confirmed that he
  reviewed the draft agreement and explained the minor changes in this draft.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN regarding the annual sports field rental
  fee, Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that the rental fee is based on the
  fee schedule approved by Council, it is currently just over $3,000 for the season, and that
  a change to this fee is not anticipated.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,

  APPROVED THE REVISED AGREEMENT WITH SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE
  FOR USE OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK'S SPORTS FIELDS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF FEBRUARY
  18, 2020 - PROPOSED MULTI-USE WATERING STATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1.) approve the donation of a multi-use water
  station by California Water Service to be placed at the northeast corner of Palos Verdes
  Drive North and Rolling Hills Road with an estimated annual water usage cost of $360;
  2.) authorize the City Manager to sign an agreement with Cal Water for the installation of
  a water station upon City Attorney review; and 3.) approve the future installation of a
  bench and hitching post as a Scout project at a cost not to exceed $500.

  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Assistant City Manager Davis confirmed that
  the Scout project is newly proposed but not yet in the works.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL expressed concern about clogging that commonly
  happens to public drinking fountains.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented on the design of the newly proposed
  fountain versus the design of those already installed throughout the City, specifically the
  desire for a water bottle filling station.

  Discussion ensued about the drain system, clogging concerns, and the maintenance of
  the drinking fountains.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith explained the rental fees paid by the City for all water fountains owned by the
  City.

  COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by,  MAYOR  PRO  TEM
  ZUCKERMAN,

  APPROVED THE DONATION OF A MULTI-USE WATER STATION BY
  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE TO BE PLACED AT THE NORTHEAST CORNER
  OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND ROLLING HILLS ROAD WITH AN
  ESTIMATED ANNUAL WATER USAGE COST OF $360; AUTHORIZED THE CITY
  MANAGER TO SIGN AN AGREEMENT WITH CAL WATER FOR THE
  INSTALLATION OF A WATER STATION UPON CITY ATTORNEY REVIEW; AND
  APPROVED THE FUTURE INSTALLATION OF A BENCH AND HITCHING POST
  AS A SCOUT PROJECT AT A COST NOT TO EXCEED $500.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF FEBRUARY
  18, 2020 - COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT DRAFT SURVEY

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the draft survey and provide feedback
  and direction to staff.

  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  Discussion ensued regarding revisions and adjustments to the proposed draft survey.
  Following discussion and with COUNCIL concurrence, the following input was provided:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
   DIRECTION GIVEN TO STAFF TO MAKE THE FOLLOWING REVISIONS AND
  ADDITIONS TO THE DRAFT SURVEY: ADDITION OF “IS THERE IS ANY OTHER
  PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT THE COMMUNITY WISHES TO SEE?”; ADDITION
  OF SUGGESTIONS TO IMPROVE THE CURRENT PROGRAMS OR EVENTS
  OFFERED, ALLOWING FOR OPEN-ENDED ANSWERS AT THE END OF EACH
  SECTION; UNDER COMMUNITY PROGRAMS, CHANGE WORDING TO “WHICH
  OF THE FOLLOWING PROGRAMS WOULD YOU BE INTERESTED IN”, AS TO
  NOT IMPLY THAT THE CITY WOULD NECESSARILY BE OFFERING THESE
  PROGRAMS.

OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Don Davis updated the Council on the draft Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) ordinance
being introduced to the Planning Commission next week.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported as a member of the Regional Council and Legislative
Committee for Southern California Association of Governments, on her visit to Sacramento to
discuss Housing with various legislators.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced the Neighborhood Watch Leadership group meeting that
will be held on March 3 at 6:00 pm at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF clarified that the SBCCOG’s Board of Director’s meeting on
February 27 will be held at Redondo Beach City Hall, not the Torrance Library.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also announced the two Cox Communications Community Meetings
that will be held on February 27 at 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm at Hesse Park.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that she will be speaking on a panel at the SBCCOG’s
General Assembly on March 19 in Carson.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEVE ZUCKERMAN reported on a SBCCOG Ad Hoc Committee he is on
with City Manager Greg Grammer to discuss its membership due structure, and voiced concerns
about the current structure’s lack of equitability.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  REQUEST TO ATTEND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ASSOCIATION OF
  GOVERNMENTS: 2020 REGIONAL CONFERENCE & GENERAL ASSEMBLY - MAY 6-
  8, 2020

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN,

  AUTHORIZED ANY COUNCIL MEMBER TO ATTEND THIS FORUM.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
 OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported that with the help of staff, the City’s Home Owners Associations
(HOAs) have been contacted to let them know that she would be available to attend and speak
on City-related topics at any HOAs that are interested, in an effort to continue the collaboration
and partnerships with the associations and community. At this time, she will be attending
meetings with Ranchview, Dapplegray and Montecillo HOAs.

COUNCIL MEMBER FRANK ZERUNYAN will be speaking at the upcoming Rollingwood HOA
meeting on new housing legislation.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEVE ZUCKERMAN announced that the next City Council meeting on
March 10 will be a Policy Development & Strategic Planning Session, beginning at 3:00 pm at
Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, and encouraged all interest residents to attend.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

ADJOURNMENT

At 8:43 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting. The next City Council
meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 10, 2020 at 3:00 pm in the Council Chamber at Rolling
Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California, for an
Adjourned meeting for the purpose of a Policy Development and Strategic Planning Session.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 25, 2020
